articles.title: ‘How on earth is this man not sweating?’ Director Brett Morgen’s painstaking 10-year remaser Bowie’s ‘greatest filmed performance’
articles.summary: Moonage Daydream director Brett Morgan has turned lost footage of two 1978 concerts into an arena spectacular. ‘You can feel the danger and excitement’, he says. • ‘Lost’ 1978 David Bowie tour film to play arenas in 2027, remastered by Moonage Daydream director Brett Morgen.
body: I n 2017, when Brett Morgen began work on his acclaimed 2022 David Bowie documentary, Moonage Daydream, he was given complete access to the late star’s entire, cavernous archive. “My eyes were immediately drawn to a stack of gleaming 35mm cans with the word ‘Stage’ written on them,” he remembers.

At first, the director – whose work also includes Kurt Cobain: Montage of Heck and the Rolling Stones documentary Crossfire Hurricane – assumed the cans might contain some sort of footage shot around Bowie’s 1978 live album, Stage, recorded in mostly in Philadelphia. However, he soon realised they actually contained the holy grail of Bowie artefacts: footage of the legendary Earl’s Court shows later that year, which had remained unseen for almost 50 years. “Making Moonage Daydream, I had access to every filmed performance in existence of David Bowie,” he says, “but when I saw this one I knew this was without question the greatest filmed performance of his career.”
points: Moonage Daydream director Brett Morgan has turned lost footage of two 1978 concerts into an arena spectacular. ‘You can feel the danger and excitement’, he says.

articles.title: Elon Musk’s AI Odyssey review – the dullest, most pointless riposte possible to Christopher Nolan’s brilliant epic
articles.summary: It is hardly a shock that Grok AI’s interpretation of Homer is as meaningless as a laptop screensaver. The only surprise would be if Musk accepted defeat graciously. Which he won’t. Think back.
body: Think back. Do you remember when Elon Musk, in a weird online tantrum, and without having seen the film, condemned the supposed wokery in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, for getting Elliot Page to play Sinon and Lupita Nyong’o to play Helen of Troy? As the plaudits and the box-office receipts for Nolan’s Odyssey piled stratospherically up, Musk showed that being a good loser is not among his qualities. He petulantly exclaimed that he could do his own better and more authentic Odyssey on Grok AI. And now he has released the first online seven-minute “episode” to a world that has long since forgotten about this claim and didn’t care in the first place.

articles.title: ’40 Watts From Nowhere’: How a Feisty Pirate Radio Station Stormed the Airwaves in 1990s Silver Lake With Help From the Red Hot Chili Peppers and More
articles.summary: The 1990s were a very different time — especially in Silver Lake, California — once a fertile neighborhood of artists and musicians and now a pricey hot spot. Three decades ago, the indie music scene was flourishing with homegrown acts like Beck and Rilo Kiley, based around clubs like Spaceland and…
body: The mystique of the scrappy station is told in the new documentary “ 40 Watts From Nowhere,” a fond look back at the Silver Lake music scene and the bands and personalities that came through KBLT. The doc premiered at Slamdance in February and, thanks to Jack Black stepping in as executive producer, it got the attention of Amazon Prime, where begins streaming Tuesday.

KBLT was the brainchild of Sue Carpenter, a journalist and music lover who learned about a “legal bubble” that enabled people to start low-power radio stations without prohibitively expensive FCC licenses. Carpenter learned how to put such a station together from Berkeley, California pirate radio guru Stephen Dunifer, got help building a transmitter, and started her first radio project, KPBJ, in her San Francisco apartment. After moving to L.A., Carpenter (using a pseudonym) selected another food-themed acronym and started making connections to line up DJs.

articles.title: Arnie & Barney review – dimwit ant double-act from Maya the Bee are on mission to entertain
articles.summary: From the ugly design to the lacklustre script, this is one parents might want to skip this half-term holiday. In 1912 in Germany, antisemitic writer Waldemar Bonsels published The Adventures of Maya the Bee, which later became a 1970s anime series in Japan called Maya the Honey Bee, and was later…
body: The film opens very much in media res, with a young female bee flying through outer space clutching a small pig and droplet of water the size of her head. She’s being pursued aggressively by a handful of wasp-type creatures and a narrator solemnly intones: “Sometimes the most unlikely heroes … become legends.” The bee then stops next to a couple of red ants and asks what they’re doing. They are the narrators, they explain, but this his is all soon revealed as fantasy – the pair of ants are telling a story to a larger platoon of ants. Some exposition follows about the ants’ mission: to find fresh water.

This is fine as far as it goes, perhaps, but what a précis can’t convey is quite how staggeringly ugly and uninteresting the whole endeavour is. It starts with the character design: it’s hard to imagine any but the most aesthetically starved children embracing this ant pair. Boy are they a chore to spend time with, both visually and in terms of the lacklustre script. Even if you are struggling for entertainment options you might want to do the kids a favour and skip this one.

articles.title: Lisa Rinna, Phaedra Parks, Dolores Catania and More ‘Real Housewives’ to Star in Revival of Neil Simon’s ‘Rumors’
articles.summary: Lisa Rinna, Phaedra Parks and Dolores Catania are among the Bravo’s “Real Housewives” stars who are uniting for a new Off-Broadway revival of Neil Simon’s farce “Rumors.” They will be joined by Stacey Rusch, Cynthia Bailey, Eileen Davidson, Carole Radziwill and Candiace Dillard-Bassett.
body: Written by Simon, the acclaimed playwright of “The Odd Couple,” Sweet Charity,” Promises, Promises” and dozens more, “Rumors” revolves around a swanky soirée that spirals out of control. Here’s the official logline: “Reality was just rehearsal. When four couples gather for a party in a wealthy New York suburb, they expect champagne, revelry, and a night of good fun. Instead, they find their host in an alarming state, his wife missing, and the police on their way. Talk about a dinner party from hell!” Christine Baranski, Jessica Walter, Joyce Van Patten and Lisa Banes led in the original production, which opened on Broadway in November 1988.

The revival, which will have a limited run at the Newman Mills Theater at the Robert W. Wilson MCC Theater Space, will be directed by Zhailon Levingston, a recent Tony Award winner for “Cats: The Jellicle Ball.” Performances will begin on Jan. 9 ahead of opening night on Jan. 25, 2027.

articles.title: BAFTA Names Hilary Rosen as Chair
articles.summary: BAFTA has confirmed that Hilary Rosen has been appointed as its new chair. Following a year as deputy chair, Rosen succeeds Sara Putt, who steps down after a three-year term.
body: A BAFTA television committee member since 2021 and later its chair, she helped shape the TV and Craft Awards and oversee their juries. Outside BAFTA, Rosen is director of commissioning at UKTV, leading its slate of original scripted and unscripted content.
Rosen will be supported by Ade Rawcliffe and Andrew Miller as deputy chairs of the academy. They will serve a two-year term.

After an election, the following folks have been appointed to the board of trustees: Charu Desdot and Caroline Levy are the chairs for BAFTA’s games and television committees, while Nahrein Kemp will take up the role of LIT committee chair.
Additionally, Shrina Shah, chair of the governance and appointments committee, will join the BAFTA board of trustees.

articles.title: ‘If a person isn’t conscious, they’re not saying yes’: Cynthia Erivo on her searing new film about sexual assault
articles.summary: In Prima Facie, she plays a rising-star barrister, well versed in defending men accused of sexual violence. Then she is raped by a colleague, and her world implodes. Erivo talks about the potential impact of the film – and how she is navigating her stratospheric success.
body: Cynthia Erivo is contemplating her favourite crisps, the ridged American brand Ruffles, as we sit talking in a quiet corner of a west London restaurant. Dressed all in black and sporting her signature elongated nails, she is known for her healthy lifestyle, but everyone, it seems, has their vices. “Ruffles are just perfect,” she says. “When you get a good batch, and the salt-to-potato ratio is perfect … it’s amazing.”

She has flown in this morning to promote her new film, the legal drama Prima Facie, an adaptation of the one-woman Suzie Miller play about sexual assault, in which Jodie Comer wowed audiences in 2022. Erivo bristles when I ask if she was hesitant about picking up a role so associated with someone else. “I get asked that question a lot,” she says. The pair actually met at a fashion dinner and spoke about the role – “Not asking any tips or anything” – and Erivo insists she was always going to make Tessa her own. “I’m never worried about what someone else has done,” she says. “I try to be respectful.”

articles.title: Russell Brand told police he never had non-consensual sex
articles.summary: His trial hears statements he gave to police between 2023 and 2025, denying allegations against him.
body: Russell Brand told police in interviews in response to allegations of rape and sexual assault that he had never engaged in "non-consensual sexual activity", a court has heard.
Brand, 51, was interviewed four times between 2023 and 2025 by officers.
The TV and media personality is currently on trial at Southwark Crown Court in London on three counts of rape and other offences. He denies all the charges.

Jurors heard on Tuesday that he gave a prepared statement in each of the police interviews. In November 2023, he said: "I have repeatedly stated publicly and written extensively that I led a very promiscuous life, that I have spent years openly denouncing. I have never engaged in non-consensual activity."

articles.title: Unnamed celebrity accused of 'inappropriate sexual activities', court hears
articles.summary: The man is asking the High Court to prevent two news organisations from publishing the allegations.
body: A celebrity has asked the High Court to prevent two news organisations from publishing his identity and allegations that he abused his status for many years to engage, or attempt to engage, in "inappropriate sexual activities with a large number of girls and young women".
The unnamed celebrity is seeking an injunction, and his legal team told the first day of a trial on Tuesday that any publication would "highly likely lead him to commit suicide".
They told the court that his drastic reaction was not because of any wrongdoing, but because of the fear of "trial by media".
The man denies abusing "his power and position as a celebrity to contact and forge relationships with young women and teenagers to try to have sex with them", the court heard.

articles.title: Excellent Ensemble Hones Philly Accents, Thriller Tension in Apple’s “Nocturne”
articles.summary: Top-notch production values, a remarkable ensemble, and sharp thriller plotting allow “Nocturne” to escape the shadow of its obvious influences.
body: The Lecter of this scenario is Jurek Walter ( Stephen Graham, turning that “Adolescence” acclaim into more high-profile work), a notorious serial killer who is introduced essentially talking the patient in the room next to him into killing himself by bashing his head against the wall. Much like Hannibal could talk his Miggs into doing the unthinkable, Walter seems to have an almost supernatural gift for persuasion, making the facility’s newest nurse, Karl ( Rory Culkin ), an easy target for getting what he wants done on the outside.

While this is happening, a boy who was kidnapped years ago suddenly reappears, dazed and confused on a Pennsylvania bridge. Long presumed a victim of Walter’s, the boy’s reemergence sets in motion an investigation not only into where he’s been but whether the sister who was abducted at the same time might also still be alive. How did the child survive if Walter was in jail? And who let him go?
